description: Storing weights (and sometimes the KV cache) with fewer bits, using per-block scales: 8-bit, 4-bit or less. Less memory and faster decoding, some quality loss.
The single-file model format of ggml/llama.cpp: quantized weights plus tokenizer, chat template and metadata.
4-bit weight quantization methods for GPUs that use calibration data to decide how to round with minimal error.
Keys and values stored per token, per layer, for every active sequence. Per token: 2 × layers × KV heads × head dimension × bytes. Grows with context × concurrency.
Weights (parameters × bytes per weight) + KV cache + runtime overhead. Decides which GPU, how many users and how long a context.
Local runtimes for laptops, CPUs and edge devices, built around GGUF, with OpenAI-compatible APIs.
High-throughput GPU servers: continuous batching, PagedAttention (vLLM), RadixAttention prefix reuse (SGLang), multi-LoRA serving.
Single-stream decoding reads every weight once per token, so tokens per second ≈ bandwidth ÷ weight bytes.
